prompt:
Generate one single 16:9 frame from a gritty live-action historical film set in the Caribbean in the 1770s. This is an ENVIRONMENT SHOT: the weather and physical place are the subject. Natural photographic depth, ordinary imperfect exposure, humid surfaces, restrained color, slight organic grain. It must feel like a real place under weather, not a polished concept-art illustration or a tourist brochure. Authentic period materials: rough limewashed masonry, aged timber, wood shingles, small clay tiles, hemp rope, dirt or worn stone, tropical vegetation. No modern roads, concrete infrastructure, electricity poles, cars, engines, steel containers, corrugated sheet metal, rubber tyres, plastic, modern ships, modern roof sheeting, or visible cameras/aircraft. No fantasy castle, no pirate theme park, no oil-painting composition, no orange-and-teal grading, no gold light, no dramatic spotlight beams, no giant lightning bolt, no tornado, no tsunami, no fiery destruction. No caption, writing, logo, watermark graphic, split screen or collage. A continuous plausible space with useful physical details and a specific weather moment. This is a first frame for a restrained 10–12 second cinematic environmental shot; keep moving phenomena at a believable scale rather than frozen gigantic action.

An EYE-LEVEL WIDE SHOT of the morning AFTER a severe Caribbean windstorm in the 1770s. It has stopped raining but the sky is still pale gray; no sudden golden sunrise, no smoke or dramatic light beams. A crooked muddy village lane bends left through simple low limewashed and rough timber houses. Near right: part of one small house's wooden roof has peeled away and a few rough rafters lean inward; the rest of the wall and house remain standing. Near left: a banana trunk has snapped and lies diagonally into the gutter, with shredded dark wet leaves pressed into mud. A few wooden shingles and roof tiles, one broken plain clay pot, dirty standing water, wet washing cloth tangled on a low fence. DAMAGE IS LOCAL AND UNEVEN, not every house flattened, no field of tidy decorative wreckage. At the far end of the lane, two tiny ordinary inhabitants in worn period linen quietly lift one long fallen branch together, smaller than five percent of image height, not recognizable portraits and not looking at camera. Their presence must remain subordinate to the environment; no injured bodies, crowd, rescue drama or staged grieving. Window shutters are dull blue-green, ochre limewash washed pale, exposed wood dark from soaking. A cool humid stillness after the noise, imperfect framing as if the observer has just stepped outside to see what remains. Keep the road, roofs and fallen vegetation in one coherent depth; natural lens rendering and soft distant detail.
